subject: food-technology
title: Effects of Cooking
welcome_lead: What heat does to protein, starch and structure.
meta_desc: KS3 food: protein denaturation, starch gelatinisation.
final_note: Cooking changes food chemically and physically.

concepts.def: Protein sets solid — like cooked egg.
Starch swells and thickens with hot liquid.
Browning of starch from dry heat.

walkthroughs.body_html: When you heat an egg the clear protein turns white and solid — this is denaturation and coagulation. Once cooked it can't go back to runny.
Stir flour into hot milk — it thickens. This is gelatinisation — starch grains swelling. Toast browning is dextrinisation — starch browning under dry heat.
The brown crust on steak, toast, and roast potatoes? That's the Maillard reaction — protein and sugar browning above 140°C. It's where flavour lives.

mcqs.q: An egg setting solid when cooked is.

options: The egg shell breaking when boiled.
Proteins denaturing and bonding to form a solid structure when heated.

mcqs.q: What temperature range is the food 'danger zone'?
options: 5 to 63 degrees Celsius - where most bacteria multiply rapidly.
